gaps.sentence: Your contract will ___ for a further twelve months.
gaps.explanation: After 'will', passive = be + past participle: will be renewed.

gaps.sentence: The new stadium ___ by the end of the decade.
gaps.explanation: 'By the end of the decade' needs future perfect passive: will have been + completed. The stadium is completed by somebody.

gaps.sentence: The winners ___ a trophy at the closing ceremony.
gaps.hint: passive of a verb with two objects
gaps.explanation: Give somebody something → somebody is given something: future passive will be + given.

gaps.sentence: The parcels ___ (deliver) every morning before the shop opens.
gaps.explanation: Present simple passive (am/is/are + past participle) for regular, repeated actions: are delivered.

gaps.sentence: The road ___ at the moment — use the bypass.
gaps.explanation: 'At the moment' — present continuous passive: is being repaired.

gaps.sentence: She ___ (think) to be the finest violinist of her generation.
gaps.explanation: Impersonal passive: is thought to be. The thinkers are general, not stated.

gaps.sentence: By this time tomorrow, the results ___ to every candidate.
gaps.explanation: 'By this time tomorrow' requires future perfect passive: will have been + emailed.

gaps.sentence: She had her laptop ___ (repair) after the coffee spill.
gaps.explanation: Causative structure: had + her laptop + repaired. A technician performed the repair.
